overview: Evolution Mining is a leading, globally relevant Australian gold miner (ASX-listed, June fiscal year-end) that operates six mines: Cowal (NSW), Ernest Henry and Mt Rawdon (Queensland), Mungari (WA), Red Lake (Ontario, Canada), and an 80%-owned interest in Northparkes (NSW). The company has transformed from a pure gold producer into a gold-copper miner, with copper (via Ernest Henry and Northparkes) now a meaningful earnings and cash-flow contributor alongside gold. FY2026 revenue reached A$5.56 billion and statutory NPAT A$1.48 billion, both records, on gold production of ~715koz and copper production of ~66kt at an industry-leading AISC of A$1,717/oz.

business_model.summary: Evolution sells gold doré/bullion and gold-copper concentrate under long-term offtake arrangements, generating revenue predominantly from spot/contract sales of gold with copper and silver as valuable by-products that structurally lower AISC (Ernest Henry and Northparkes both report negative AISC per ounce of gold due to copper credits). Revenue is transactional/commodity-price-driven rather than recurring, though production volumes are relatively predictable given mine plans and reserves. The Northparkes acquisition (FY25) added a gold-copper stream arrangement with Triple Flag International, since renegotiated on more favourable terms.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - bullion sold to refiners/bullion banks; concentrate sold under offtake contracts to smelters/traders
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia (Cowal NSW, Ernest Henry & Mt Rawdon QLD, Mungari WA, Northparkes NSW) ~82% of production; Canada (Red Lake, Ontario) ~18% of gold production, FY26

competitive_position.market_position: One of Australia's largest gold producers and among the lowest-cost, highest-margin gold-copper miners globally; FY26 AISC of A$1,717/oz is well below ASX peer Northern Star (~A$2,160-2,651/oz) due to substantial copper by-product credits at Ernest Henry and Northparkes.

moat_factors.description: Ernest Henry and Northparkes generate negative AISC per gold ounce because copper/silver credits more than offset mining costs, giving Evolution structurally lower group AISC than gold-only peers and outsized operating leverage to both gold and copper prices.

moat_factors.factor: Cowal as a Tier-1 cash engine
moat_factors.description: Cowal delivered record FY26 net mine cash flow of A$851.7m; the Open Pit Continuation (OPC) project extends mine life with four new pits on budget (A$430m) and on schedule.

Moved to a net cash position in FY26 (A$1,347.5m cash vs A$1,380.6m gross debt after early term-loan repayment), an investment-grade private credit rating, undrawn A$525m RCF, and no debt maturities before FY29 - unusual flexibility among mid-cap gold miners.
Geographic and orebody diversification across Australia and Canada reduces single-asset risk versus smaller peers, though scale remains below Newmont/Northern Star.

Recognised by Sustainalytics, MSCI, S&P CSA and Dow Jones Best-in-Class indices; supports social licence to operate and lowers regulatory/community friction, particularly relevant for permitting new pits and underground expansions.

weaknesses: Rising AISC trend (A$907/oz FY2016 to A$1,717/oz FY2026, guided to A$1,795-1,995/oz FY2027) driven by cost inflation, royalties and lower ore grades
Declining gold production profile at legacy assets (Cowal, Ernest Henry, Northparkes, Mt Rawdon all down YoY in FY26; Mt Rawdon ceasing processing in Sep-2026 quarter)
Weather/operational disruption risk demonstrated by the Dec-2025/Mar-2026 Ernest Henry flooding event (~12koz gold, ~8kt copper, A$45.4m costs)
Sub-scale relative to Newmont post-Newcrest merger; limited global diversification outside Australia/Canada
High share-based/incentive remuneration and non-IFRS 'underlying' metrics require scrutiny versus statutory results

growth_drivers: Cowal Open Pit Continuation (OPC) project - four new adjacent open pits (E46 commenced FY26), A$430m budget over seven years, IRR 34-115% depending on gold price scenario

Northparkes E22 block cave and Coarse Particle Flotation Project, approved Feb-2026, targeting production by end-FY30; renegotiated Triple Flag stream unlocks E44 gold-rich deposit (A$120m upfront payment Dec-2026)

Ernest Henry Bert underground development, approved Feb-2026, first production FY29, plus the pending Carnaby Resources acquisition (A$213m, Greater Duchess copper-gold project) adding ~10,000tpa copper potential near Ernest Henry's existing mill
Mungari 4.2Mtpa mill expansion completed ahead of schedule/under budget (A$212m vs A$250m budget) in FY26, driving record 186koz production (+38% YoY)
Red Lake continued de-risking - record FY26 net mine cash flow of A$286.1m (20% payback of invested capital), Cochenour decline and tailings/water treatment infrastructure completed
Exploration pipeline in British Columbia (Two Times Fred, Clisbako) and a 9.9% stake in Arizona Gold & Silver (Philadelphia Gold-Silver Project, Arizona)
Unhedged gold position (final hedge delivery completed FY26) provides full leverage to further gold price gains
Secular tailwind: gold price strength (achieved price up 40% YoY to A$6,023/oz in FY26; spot ~A$7,100/oz referenced at Dec-2025) driven by central bank buying and rate-cut expectations

business.description: Must continually replace depleting reserves via exploration or M&A (JORC 2012); exploration is speculative and can take years to convert to production.
Actual grades, dilution, metallurgy, labour availability and mine sequencing can vary materially from plan, as seen with FY26 gold production of 715koz missing the internal STIP target of 760koz.
Cowal OPC, Northparkes E22/CPF, and Ernest Henry Bert are all large, multi-year capital projects; delays or cost overruns would pressure cash flow and growth guidance.
Pit wall failures, seismic events, cave-ins and weather (flooding, bushfire) are inherent to underground and open-pit mining; insurance may not fully cover losses.

financial.risk: Gold, copper and silver price volatility
financial.description: Revenue is directly exposed to spot metal prices; Evolution is now fully unhedged following final hedge delivery in FY26, removing the downside protection hedges previously provided.

Revenue is largely USD-linked (gold/copper priced in USD) while costs are AUD/CAD-denominated; US Private Placement debt (~A$1.38bn) is USD-denominated, though currency swaps largely hedge FX risk on that debt.
Labour (~half the cost base), royalties linked to higher metal prices, fuel, and consumables have driven AISC up 9% in FY26 with further 4-5% escalation guided into FY27.

regulatory.risk: Environmental, water, climate and cultural heritage regulation
regulatory.description: Extensive approvals required across Australian states and Ontario, Canada; AASB S2 climate disclosure now mandatory (first Climate Report released Aug-2026).
Failure to manage stakeholder/Indigenous partnerships could disrupt permitting, exploration and production; mitigated by Reconciliation Plan and 'High Approval' social licence survey score.
Subject to ACCC clearance, scheme/court approval and Carnaby shareholder vote (expected late Oct/early Nov 2026); completion risk though deal is friendly and well-received.

macro.description: Bank forecasts range widely ($4,000-$6,300/oz through 2027); a hawkish Fed surprise, dollar strength, or easing geopolitical tension could trigger a correction toward US$4,000-4,500/oz, which would compress margins given rising AISC.

Gold generally benefits from rate cuts (lower opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets); Evolution's own borrowing cost is fixed-rate (4.47% weighted average) with no maturities before FY29, limiting direct refinancing risk.
FY26 cost of sales increase partly attributed to higher fuel costs from Middle East tensions; broader supply-chain/input cost exposure to global geopolitical shocks.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold sector outlook remains broadly constructive: major banks (JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley) forecast gold prices continuing higher through 2026-2027 (estimates from US$4,900 to US$6,300/oz) on central bank buying, Fed rate cuts, and dollar diversification, though central bank purchase momentum slowed sharply in Q1 2026 (16 tonnes net vs ~225 tonnes/quarter 2021-2025 average) and a pullback to US$4,000-4,500/oz is a live risk scenario. Copper demand is supported by electrification/energy-transition themes, benefiting Evolution's Ernest Henry/Northparkes/Carnaby copper exposure.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - a commodity cyclical business with revenue, margins and share price directly tied to gold/copper spot prices; countercyclical to broad equities in risk-off periods given gold's safe-haven status, but production costs and capex are pro-cyclical with mining-sector wage/input inflation.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect but meaningful - lower real rates typically support gold prices (lower opportunity cost of non-yielding assets); Evolution's own debt is fixed-rate, limiting direct interest expense sensitivity.

recent_developments.event: Reported record FY26 results: statutory NPAT A$1,475.1m (+59%), underlying NPAT A$1,562.9m (+63%), record underlying EBITDA A$3,171.3m (+44%); final dividend 21.0cps (total FY26 dividend 41.0cps, +62% YoY, 27th consecutive dividend); moved to net cash position.
FY26 guidance met: 715koz gold and 66kt copper produced at AISC A$1,717/oz, within original guidance ranges despite the Ernest Henry weather event.
Announced planned retirement of Non-Executive Director Tommy McKeith and appointment of John Vann as Non-Executive Director, effective 1 December 2026.
Acquired a 9.9% equity stake in Arizona Gold & Silver Inc for A$12.1m, linked to the Philadelphia Gold-Silver Project in Arizona's Oatman Mining District.

Agreed to acquire Carnaby Resources Ltd for ~A$213m via scheme of arrangement (0.0682 EVN shares per Carnaby share), adding the Greater Duchess copper-gold project near Ernest Henry (~10,000tpa copper potential); scheme meeting expected late Oct/early Nov 2026.
Board approved Northparkes E22 block cave, Coarse Particle Flotation Project and Mill Expansion Study, and the Ernest Henry Bert underground development (first production FY29).

Extreme rainfall (~300mm in 24 hours late Dec-2025, further above-average rainfall in March 2026) caused temporary suspension of underground production at Ernest Henry; ~12koz gold and ~8kt copper production impact, A$45.4m recovery costs, insurance recoveries expected to partially offset; full production resumed at the start of the June 2026 quarter.

guidance.management_commentary: Management (CEO Lawrie Conway) emphasised that all major growth projects (Cowal OPC, Northparkes E22/CPF, Ernest Henry Bert, Mungari expansion) remained on schedule and within approved budgets through FY26, with returns on these projects expected to exceed the Group's historical average IRR since acquisition. The Board highlighted the shift to a net cash position and an unhedged gold book as evidence of balance sheet strength and full exposure to further gold price upside, while flagging FY27 AISC guidance increases as a function of cost inflation and higher sustaining capital rather than operational underperformance.

bull_case: Industry-leading cost position via copper by-product credits at Ernest Henry and Northparkes gives EVN structurally lower AISC than gold-only peers, translating record gold/copper prices into outsized margin and cash flow gains (FY26 underlying EBITDA margin 57% vs 51% in FY25)
Fully unhedged gold book (final hedges delivered FY26) provides full leverage to a gold price environment several major banks still forecast rising toward US$5,000-6,300/oz through 2027

Strong, de-risked growth pipeline (Cowal OPC, Northparkes E22/CPF, Ernest Henry Bert, plus the Carnaby/Greater Duchess copper acquisition) with disclosed project IRRs of 20-128% across base and upside price scenarios, all on schedule/budget as of FY26

Balance sheet moved to net cash in FY26 with an undrawn A$525m RCF and no debt maturities before FY29, funding growth capex and a progressive dividend (27 consecutive payments, ~60%-of-cash-flow policy) without needing equity raises
Diversification into copper (now ~22% of revenue) provides a second commodity growth driver tied to energy-transition/electrification demand, reducing pure gold-price dependence
bear_case: AISC has nearly doubled since FY2016 (A$907/oz to A$1,717/oz) and FY27 guidance steps up further to A$1,795-1,995/oz, showing structural cost inflation that could compress margins if gold/copper prices plateau or retreat

Legacy asset production is declining across the board (Cowal, Ernest Henry, Northparkes, Mt Rawdon all down YoY in FY26; Mt Rawdon ceasing entirely in Sep-2026), making FY27 group gold guidance (660-730koz) lower at the midpoint than FY26 actuals

Fully unhedged position removes the downside protection a hedge book previously offered, leaving earnings exposed to a gold price correction - several forecasters flag a plausible pullback to US$4,000-4,500/oz on a hawkish Fed surprise, dollar strength, or slowing central bank buying (Q1 2026 net purchases fell to just 16 tonnes)

Weather and operational disruption risk is demonstrated (Ernest Henry Dec-2025/Mar-2026 flooding cost ~12koz gold, ~8kt copper and A$45.4m), and the business carries multiple large, concurrent capital projects (OPC, E22/CPF, Bert) with execution/delay risk

Consensus analyst view is only 'Hold'/Neutral with price targets (~A$12.70-13.70) below the stock's March-2026 all-time high (A$17.75), suggesting the market sees much of the good news already priced in after a strong run
